claims.quote: Now she’s 30, and her private, Palo Alto-based corporation, called Theranos–the name is an amalgam of the words “therapy” and “diagnosis”–has 500 employees and has raised more than $400 million from equity sales to investors who have effectively valued the company at more than $9 billion.
claims.why: Check employee count, capital raised, valuation, and company location.

claims.quote: Theranos today is a potentially highly disruptive upstart in America’s $73 billion diagnostic-lab industry, which performs nearly 10 billion tests a year and is estimated to provide the basis for about 70% of doctors’ medical decisions.
claims.why: Verify industry size, test volume, and proportion of medical decisions influenced.

claims.quote: Medicare and Medicaid each pay roughly $10 billion annually on reimbursements for these tests.
claims.why: Check annual Medicare and Medicaid reimbursement totals for diagnostic tests.

claims.quote: Theranos runs what’s called a high-complexity laboratory, certified by the federal Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), and it is licensed to operate in nearly every state.
claims.why: Verify CMS certification status and state licensing reach.

claims.quote: It currently offers more than 200–and is ramping up to offer more than 1,000–of the most commonly ordered blood diagnostic tests, all without the need for a syringe.
claims.why: Check test menu size and absence of syringes.

claims.quote: The company has performed as many as 70 different tests from a single draw of 25 to 50 microliters collected in a tiny vial the size of an electric fuse, which Holmes has dubbed a “nanotainer.”
claims.why: Check if 70 tests from a single tiny sample volume is physically possible without independent validation.

claims.quote: Precisely how Theranos accomplishes all these amazing feats is a trade secret.
claims.why: Check whether proprietary claims block verification of core methodology.

claims.quote: Holmes will only say–and this is more than she has ever said before–that her company uses “the same fundamental chemical methods” as existing labs do.
claims.why: Check if the technical explanation is too generic for how small volumes achieve standard results.

claims.quote: Its phlebotomists currently take physician-ordered blood draws (and saliva, urine, feces, and other samples) at collection centers the company operates at its headquarters in Palo Alto and at 21 Walgreens–one in Palo Alto and the rest in Phoenix.
claims.why: Verify collection center locations and operating entities.

claims.quote: It plans to establish Theranos outposts in a substantial percentage of its 8,200 drugstores in all 50 states.
claims.why: Check Walgreens store count and rollout plans.

claims.quote: Using DNA profiling Theranos can, for less than the cost of the conventional tests, identify a bug and its resistance profile within four hours, says Helfet, according to the data he has seen.
claims.why: Check if rapid DNA profiling without independent published validation is feasible.

claims.quote: Theranos may, in fact, be the only lab to have ever sought FDA clearance for LDTs.
claims.why: Verify FDA submission records for lab-developed tests across the industry.

claims.quote: Though it has now raised more than $400 million, she says she has retained control over more than 50% of the stock.
claims.why: Check equity distribution and ownership stakes.

claims.quote: Today Holmes is a co-inventor on 82 U.S. and 189 foreign patent applications, of which 18 in the U.S. and 66 abroad have been granted.
claims.why: Verify patent application and grant totals with patent offices.
Check if pricing comparisons across independent and hospital labs hold universally.

claims.quote: Such pricing represents a potential godsend for the uninsured, the insured with high deductibles, insurers, and taxpayers.
claims.why: Assess broad assertions of economic benefit without concrete pricing data.
